 Advertisement Iowa Insurance Division offering free webinar on Medicare changes and 2027 plans
 Medicare beneficiaries and caregivers can get free guidance on plan changes, prescription costs and enrollment pitfalls during a free, public statewide webinar.
 Advertisement Updated: 10:31 PM CST Nov 10, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Iowa Insurance Division offering free webinar on Medicare changes and 2027 plans
 Medicare beneficiaries and caregivers can get free guidance on plan changes, prescription costs and enrollment pitfalls during a free, public statewide webinar.
 Updated: 10:31 PM CST Nov 10, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ , Iowa — Iowans on Medicare will have a chance to get free guidance on upcoming plan changes during a statewide virtual workshop next week.
 The Iowa Insurance Division's Senior Health Insurance Information Program and Senior Medicare Patrol, known as SHIIP-SMP, will host a 90-minute webinar Wednesday, Nov. 18, focused on navigating Medicare Open Enrollment and changes taking effect in 2027.
 Advertisement The free webinar will be held from 10:30 a.m. to noon and will be hosted online through Zoom.
 The presentation will include a demonstration of Medicare.gov's plan finder tool and cover how beneficiaries can compare plans, avoid common enrollment mistakes and find lower-cost options for prescription drugs.
 The session will also cover changes to Medicare plans taking effect next year, shifting prescription formularies and programs that may help reduce out-of-pocket prescription costs.
 The webinar is intended for Medicare beneficiaries, family caregivers, people approaching age 65 and aging-services advocates.
 Kristin Gidel, SHIIP-SMP's training and education coordinator, will lead the presentation.
 Registration is required, and attendance is limited to the first 500 participants. 
 Iowans can register for the Nov. 18 webinar through this link , the SHIIP-SMP website or call 1-800-351-4664 for more information.
 SHIIP-SMP provides free, objective and confidential Medicare counseling to Iowans. The program also helps beneficiaries identify and report Medicare errors, fraud and abuse.
